1. Payoff shape. Heliod's discount D (generic only, X counts) by T8 [MEAS]: median 4; 30% of windows 10+, 22% 15+, 16% 20+ (best-case reachable — a ceiling). D needed to pay only pips [ARITH]: Approach {6}{W} D>=6; Venser {2}{U}{U} D>=2; Remand {1}{U} D>=1; Windfall D>=2; Mathemagics X=3 (8 cards) D>=3; Psychosis Crawler {5} D>=5; Scrawling Crawler {3} D>=3; Forced Fruition D>=4; Prosperity/Fascination X=7 D>=7; Stroke X=7 D>=9; Ballista {X}{X} 2X. Ranked shapes: (a) Approach twice in one window — Approach, Venser bouncing it (combo 553-3634 on b3-v1; the first cast need not resolve), Approach again; at D>=7 the line is W+UU+W; or 7+ draws (Mathemagics X=3, Windfall, Prosperity X=7); Teferi first (stack 007). Bottleneck: Approach in hand, not the discount. (b) Draw-X into a converter: Scrawling (each opponent draw costs them 1) and Psychosis (each of our draws costs each opponent 1), each-opponent drain (strategy:conversion.yield); Prosperity or Fascination X=20 with both Crawlers is 40 to each opponent for 2 mana at D>=20; a chain from low D (Folio X=2 -> Prosperity X~11 -> Fascination X~40) needs a stack scenario and a library-size check; Crawler drain is 3.5% of kills by T10 [MEAS] because there are two Crawlers in 99 (strategy:conversion.availability, strategy:deckbuilding.redundancy-vs-tutors). call.reading: Heliod is an Approach deck; the second line is game-winning discounts. Remand joins Venser as a way to bounce our own Approach back to hand after its first cast, so the second cast wins for little mana once Heliod's discount covers it; the goldfish, taught the bounce this session, reads the line paying when its reader is removed. Triskaidekaphile adds a third win, drawing to exactly thirteen on an opponent's turn. Soul-Guide Lantern stays as the deck's only graveyard answer; Scour for Scrap was declined for want of a cut. Isochron Scepter and Sphere of Safety are invisible to the goldfish, so the cuts rest on the strategist's audit and the pilot's word.
